record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: Does any manganite compound realize a truly homogeneous spin-canted ground state without an applied magnetic field, rather than an apparently canted state that can instead be explained by phase inhomogeneity?

evidence.quote: Is there any compound with a truly spin-canted homogeneous ground state? ... experimental evidence for canting can be always alternatively explained through inhomogeneities in the ground state.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider doped perovskite manganite compounds of the form R_{1-x}A_x MnO_3 (with R a trivalent rare earth and A a divalent alkaline earth), modeled by Mn ions carrying localized t_{2g} spins coupled via Hund's rule to itinerant e_g electrons, including double-exchange, superexchange, electron-phonon and Coulomb interactions. A "homogeneous spin-canted state" means a single-phase magnetic ground state in which, in the absence of any applied magnetic field, every Mn site carries a spin tilted by the same nonzero canting angle relative to a global axis (so neighboring sublattices form a uniform, non-collinear ferro/antiferromagnetic arrangement throughout the sample). This is to be contrasted with an inhomogeneous (phase-separated) ground state consisting of coexisting ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic domains, whose macroscopic magnetization can mimic a canted state.

Question: Does there exist a manganite compound whose zero-field ground state is a truly homogeneous spin-canted state, as opposed to a phase-inhomogeneous state that merely appears canted on average?
artifact.status_search_result: Theoretical work on double-exchange models suggests the homogeneous canted state is generically unstable toward phase separation into ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic regions, and several compounds originally reported as canted antiferromagnets (e.g. bilayer manganites) were later reinterpreted as phase-separated. However, no definitive experimental proof has been found establishing a manganite with a truly homogeneous canted ground state, nor a rigorous theorem excluding it. The status appears unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Nanoscale phase separation in manganites
status_evidence.snippet: Homogeneous canted state in manganite models is unstable toward formation of small ferromagnetic droplets in an antiferromagnetic insulating matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical results argue against homogeneous canting and in favor of phase separation.

status_evidence.title: Colossal magnetoresistant materials: the key role of phase separation
status_evidence.snippet: Ground states of manganite models tend to be intrinsically inhomogeneous due to strong tendencies toward phase separation.
status_evidence.claim: Apparent canting in experiments is often reinterpreted as phase inhomogeneity.
